requirements.requirement: Build a three-member etcd cluster across node1, node2, and node3
requirements.summary: etcd v3.5.17 installed and configured on all three nodes with matching initial-cluster settings; systemd service started on all three; member list shows all three members (node1, node2, node3) with status 'started' and correct peer/client URLs, and endpoint health returns true for all three endpoints.

requirements.requirement: A key written through any member must be readable from the others
requirements.summary: A key ('foo') written via node1 was read back successfully on node2 and node3; a key ('fromnode2') written via node2 was read back on node1 and node3; a key ('fromnode3') written via node3 was read back on node1 and node2, directly demonstrating full-mesh replication.

requirements.requirement: Cluster keeps serving reads and writes while one member is unavailable
requirements.summary: node3's etcd was stopped and confirmed inactive; with node3 down, endpoint health for node1/node2 remained true, and a new key ('duringoutage') was successfully written and read back against the two remaining members, directly demonstrating continued availability during a bounded single-member disruption.

requirements.requirement: Bring the unavailable member back up to date when it returns
requirements.summary: node3's etcd was restarted, and after restart it reported healthy status, returned the keys written while it was down ('duringoutage', 'foo'), and endpoint status showed identical raft term/index/applied-index (2/20/20) across all three members, directly demonstrating successful resynchronization.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol on node1 (pre-restart baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state)
requirements.summary: Pre-reboot boot_id (bf4e9cbb...) and healthy etcd/cluster state captured; systemctl reboot issued (stream closed indicates the reboot took effect, consistent with subsequent connection timeouts); post-reboot boot_id (096cd853...) confirms a genuinely new boot, matching the fixed after_executor snapshot; etcd active again with cluster health true, member list intact, and key 'foo' readable.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol on node2
requirements.summary: Pre-reboot boot_id (6bb7e004...) and healthy etcd/cluster state captured; reboot issued and acknowledged; post-reboot boot_id (11c2ea15...) confirms a new boot, matching the fixed after_executor snapshot; etcd active again, cluster health true across all endpoints, member list intact, key 'foo' present.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol on node3 (final cycle, full quorum recovery)
requirements.summary: Pre-reboot boot_id (fbdf5b2c...) and healthy etcd/cluster state captured; reboot issued and acknowledged; post-reboot boot_id (119506f3...) confirms a new boot, matching the fixed after_executor snapshot; etcd active again, cluster health true, all previously written keys present, and endpoint status shows matching raft term/index/applied-index (5/38/38) across all three members, confirming full cluster recovery and quorum.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct, first-hand evidence: a healthy 3-member etcd cluster was formed, cross-member read/write consistency was demonstrated for all three nodes, the cluster continued serving reads/writes with node3 stopped, and node3 fully resynchronized (matching raft indices) upon return. The independent provider-wide restart protocol was also executed correctly and sequentially (preserving quorum) for all three nodes, with clear pre/post boot-id changes and full post-restart cluster/data/quorum recovery, cross-checked against the fixed after_executor snapshot. The only hygiene concern is unremoved temporary etcd release archives/binaries left in /tmp on each node, a low-risk but unnecessary residue.
limitations: Package-health baseline was unavailable (timed out) at before_prepare, so no package-manager consistency comparison across the full lifecycle was possible; only the after_executor observation could be used.

The reboot 'acknowledgement' evidence relies on an exec-stream-closed error plus subsequent connection timeouts rather than an explicit systemd reboot confirmation message, though this is a reasonable and commonly used proxy given the node becomes unreachable immediately after.

operational_hygiene.summary: Executor's state-changing actions (package install, user/data-dir creation, config/unit-file writes, firewall port opens, service starts, member outage test, sequential reboots) all map directly to task requirements or the mandated restart protocol; the initial node1 systemctl enable --now failure during bootstrap (cmd-00ebb17380d949e7, rc=3) is an expected transient timeout while waiting for peers to join a fresh 3-node cluster, not a lingering fault, and it self-resolved (cmd-6122366e7f48400e shows active). The one notable hygiene gap is leftover build artifacts (/tmp/etcd.tar.gz and the extracted etcd-v3.5.17-linux-amd64 directory) retained on all three nodes after installation, visible in the after_executor temporary-files diff; this is low-risk residue (plain release binaries/docs, not secrets) but was never cleaned up. No failed services, conflicting units, unsafe new exposure beyond the required etcd ports, or damaged package state were observed (after_executor package-health reports a healthy dnf manager on all nodes, and failed-services lists are empty on all nodes).
